title: What is the best 'vanilla' RPG Maker game to have been made? Seeking opinions and examples

posts.author: hatesec
posts.body:
I'm curious what you guys may have come across in your years developing with RPG Maker. I suspect that there have been some seriously good writers come across this software, made a game with it, and released it with vanilla assets, maybe just to showcase their writing or storytelling abilities, or battle system ideas, but within the confines of the RTP.
In the roughly 600 hours I've spent in RMMZ, I've formed an unexpected affinity for the software. I'm still working on my first game, very happy with how it's coming along, and of course I use several plugins to bridge the gaps between my vision and what the engine comes ready to do. I created much of my game assets and content in photoshop, audacity, and so on. You know how it is.
In the back of my mind, though, as I've fallen in love with the software, I've been playing with the idea of beginning work on a second game once this one is finished. The idea is that I'd like to see what I can do in RMMZ without the use of any plugins, GALV layers, or even sound editing, leaning heavily on the writing, further exploring the possibilities of the RTP, and offering up a proper battle system.
To that end, I'll be pursuing challenges such as: How detailed can I make my maps? How can I innovate on the battle system? Can I carry that play experience through good writing, characterization, character development, and a proper circular narrative arc?
I have a vision of elegantly delivering a warm play experience using the default assets, perhaps by lending life and character to the default faces we've all seen and got sick of by now. Maybe I'll cheat a little and use the DF and MVT assets for which I've already acquired licenses, but retain that RPG Maker look, with the hope of surprising someone with the material itself.
You guys seen any impressive examples of what I'm talking about? Anything that looked basic, or unpolished, yet surprised you?

posts.author: TRIDIUM
posts.body:
IDK, if I saw a game on my itch or steam feed that looked basic and unpolished, I wouldn't really want to play it
But since I do play quite a few RM games here, I don't think I've ever played an 100% RTP no plugins or anything game that I was particularly impressed by.
I think you're onto something here, however.
I wouldn't limit myself to the RTP, but that notion of focusing on core things are relying on good writing and mechanics is good. I would say that visual storytelling and a good art direction can be really helpful when telling a story, but hey, not necessary.
However, don't expect to get many people to play it. If your game doesn't look interesting, it doesn't matter how good it is, most people still won't play it. You'd be relying on word of mouth, essentially.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
The two are basically equivalent. Take an MV sample game and plop in the tilesets and character sprites from MZ if you like.
The changes to the editor and code in MZ are primarily enhancements on the developer's side. The only real change that one could observe from playing a basic RTP game, besides the different assets as above, is the Effekseer animations.

posts.author: firestalker
posts.body:
I remember.... way back in the day.... *cough* *cough* before RPG Maker was in English. There was an RPG Maker XP "game" that I loved and waited patiently for the next installments as they were released. I can't remember the exact name, but it was something like "Masters of the Wind"...  It started the RPG maker "Game that isn't a game" craze from about a decade ago.
The game was just a show, the whole thing was cutscenes one after another that told a story. there were episodes and everything. I think it eventually just died, but it was very well done and used mostly the generic RTP graphics [with some modifications later on].
There were several "games" that were released around that time with similar MOs and I loved the creativity and storytelling.

posts.author: garahad-ser
posts.body:
"Vanilla" rpgmaker isn't objectively boring.  It's only "boring" to people who have seen it many times before.
Like, if Final Fantasy started using the FF1 assets for all their games, that would be "boring" too.
Which is not to damn the vanilla, but exonerate it.  The games quality has nothing to do with the assets.  A game is fun if it's fun.  Simple.
Of course, people will always prejudge regardless, and that's the issue.
But you know what?  If you're always trying to make a game to appeal to others, you may forget to appeal to you, and unless you're specifically commissioned or contracted to make a game to another's brief, why risk making it unfun for you?

posts.author: TotalyNate
posts.body:
I agree with
@garahad-ser
, in my opinion you can make a good game with 100% rtp resources, a game is GOOD if it's GOOD, I have seen some games where the music is amazing and the maps are amazing, but the story isn't there, and it makes me not want to play it, you could spend 600 hours on a game with the rtp and it would be just as good as a game with custom graphics and music, if the story was good. I only like to use a few plugins in my games, (10 or less) because I generally like the music and the graphics, now you do you, but no one should judge a game just because it uses the rtp.
(Not to mention most of players don't know about rpg maker when they get a game, so they don't know you're using "rtp")

posts.author: Xaniro
posts.body:
TRIDIUM said:
IDK, if I saw a game on my itch or steam feed that looked basic and unpolished, I wouldn't really want to play it
Click to expand...
You won't want to play it, because you are a person who uses the program that creates that game. The game creators don't make the game for the people on this forum to play it, they make it so that as many people as possible play it. The creators of the game are a minority compared to the number of people who are looking for a game on android or steam or any other place where it can be played.
If you tell a friend that you are a game creator and show them screenshots of a game created with RPG MAKER MV with the default graphics and without plugins, they would be fascinated and impressed with how great the game is and they will play it because they do not have any knowledge of what is basic and good work in the RPG MAKER program.
The risk you run when making the game with the default resources offered by the program is that it could look similar to other games also created with RPG MAKER with the default resources. And that will probably make people see it as something normal and not something that they will be tempted to play.
